paragraphs.text: Lancaster III PB366 (TL-S) of 35 Squadron, a Pathfinder squadron, took off from Graveley at 15:35 on 24 December 1944 for Cologne. Ten of the squadron's aircraft were detailed to attack the Nippes Marshalling Yard. PB366's Pathfinder role was Supporter.

FIDO fog dispersal was burning at take-off. PB366 crashed almost immediately, flying into trees at Great Paxton. The squadron-association page puts the crash site at Low Farm, about half a mile south of the aerodrome. AM Form 1180 blamed the pilot losing control in fog through faulty instrument flying. All seven crew died.

The bombs were thrown clear of the wreck. One rolled into the wall of the farmhouse bathroom at Low Farm, with the farmer's wife inside, and did not explode. A man on the Graveley crash guard reached the scene a few minutes later and found the aircraft burning.

The crew were Flying Officer Arthur Kenyon (pilot, 23), Sergeant Leonard Williams (flight engineer, 23), Sergeant Albert Thomas (navigator, 22), Flight Sergeant Alec Cousins (bomb aimer, 21), Flight Sergeant Cecil Blundell (wireless operator, 20), Sergeant Cyril Winter (mid-upper gunner, 23) and Sergeant Roy Yallop (rear gunner, 24). Their burial places run from Prestwich and Staveley to Ystalyfera, Maidenhead, Southampton, Harlington and Ipswich. Thomas's age is given by Aircrew Remembered only; IBCC and CWGC do not state it, and the Graveley PDF shows a question mark.
Yallop had flown as a gunner with the Potts crew on the Gremberg daylight raid on 23 December, the day before he died. His family received the telegram on Christmas morning.

The cross is a plain white wooden cross, about 1.2 m high, at the junction of Dovecote Lane and High Street (B1043) in Great Paxton. The cross member reads LANCASTER CRASH 1944, and a board beneath gives the date, the aircraft, the crew names and 35 Squadron. IWM records it in good condition. IWM gives no maker or date for it, and none of the other sources read says who put it up.

notes: Conflicts and cautions. (1) Yallop's middle names: IBCC, 35 Squadron site and Aircrew Remembered give Roy Frederick Arthur; the Graveley PDF gives Roy Arthur. Same man, variant claim recorded. (2) Albert Thomas's age is 22 only from Aircrew Remembered (single source); IBCC and CWGC show no age, the Graveley PDF a question mark. (3) Crew roles for Cousins, Winter and Yallop (bomb aimer, mid-upper, rear gunner) rest on Aircrew Remembered only; IBCC says Air Bomber / Air Gunner. (4) Material of the pillar: IWM says Clipsham stone; Hunts Post planning report (S17) says granite from a Cornish quarry. Not used in paragraphs because Hunts Post is secondary; it may be the proposed rather than final stone. (5) Original plan reported in Hunts Post (S16) was a steel Lancaster sculpture in Dovecote Lane; the memorial built is the eagle pillar in the churchyard. (6) Crash location varies: Low Farm about half a mile south of Graveley aerodrome (S3, S4); Hunts Post says a field near what is now Brookside after clipping a house on London Lane. (7) Hunts Post and 35 Squadron site say unveiling 7 May 2022; Aircrew Remembered's earlier note said 14:00 at the church, unconfirmed. CWGC: only the Thomas page was fetched; the other six cwgc_url claims are built from casualty numbers printed on their IBCC pages (URL pattern confirmed by the Thomas page). Burial section wording is from IBCC. Nationality is IBCC 'country of origin' (United Kingdom), all RAFVR; no source states a nationality outright. Hometowns are from next-of-kin lines (Aircrew Remembered/Graveley PDF). IWM names lists on both register pages are empty, so the stone's name spellings could not be checked. Aircrew Remembered and the Graveley PDF may share origin; the 35 Squadron site and Great Paxton site are separate publishers. Paxtons benefice newsletter (S19, community tier, undated about 2019-20) says a white cross and silhouette were at Dovecote Lane and would 'remain in place' until the memorial was built; used only here. Custodian: nothing read names a custodian for either memorial, so custodian_status is 'unknown' (searched, no source either way), not 'unknown-confirmed'. The History Society built the pillar; the parish council supported planning (S17); neither is stated to maintain it. Contact details exist in S19 for private individuals and were deliberately not recorded. The IWM record's own inscription for the pillar and cross are as on IWM. Existing record contradictions: none found; our pillar record has an empty squadron field (35 Squadron per sources). Memorial leads not followed: IBCC Digital Archive accident form, War Memorials Online, Find a Grave pages, the video on the History Society page.
